title: CROSS JOIN & Cartesian Products
description: Generate Cartesian products, create matrix combinations (sizes x colors), and avoid accidental performance catastrophes.

data.text: A **`CROSS JOIN`** produces the Cartesian product of two tables. Every row from Table A is paired with every row from Table B. If Table A contains 10 rows and Table B contains 50 rows, the resulting table contains exactly 10 × 50 = 500 rows.
Practical Use: Generating Product Variant SKUs

data.title: Generating All Size and Color Combinations
data.content: Permuting attributes to generate inventory SKU matrices.
data.code:
SELECT 
    p.name AS product_name,
    s.size_label,
    c.color_name,
    CONCAT(p.code, '-', s.size_code, '-', c.color_code) AS generated_sku
FROM products p
CROSS JOIN sizes s
CROSS JOIN colors c
WHERE p.is_active = true;

data.title: Accidental Cartesian Explosion
data.text: Never omit the `ON` condition in an old-style comma join (`FROM table_a, table_b`)! If Table A has 100,000 rows and Table B has 100,000 rows, an accidental CROSS JOIN computes 10,000,000,000 rows, exhausting database memory and crashing production!

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `CROSS JOIN` multiplies the cardinality of both tables (M × N).
Useful for calendar day filling, permutations, and SKU matrix generation.
Always use explicit `CROSS JOIN` syntax rather than comma joins.
